chunks: And Thamud and the people of Lot and the dwellers of the Wood, those were the hordes.

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الْأَيْكَةِ: The dwellers of the Wood, a people mentioned in the Quran who denied Prophet Shu'ayb
key_terms.الْأَحْزَابُ: The hordes or parties, referring to groups of disbelievers
key_terms.صَمُودُ: Thamud, an ancient Arab tribe known for their denial of Prophet Salih
key_terms.قَوْمُ لُوطٍ: The people of Lot, known for their sexual immorality and denial of Prophet Lot

ai.seo_question: Who are the three groups referred to as 'the hordes' in Surah Sad?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to illustrate the collective nature of divine punishment against distinct yet similarly obstinate communities, reinforcing the concept of 'al--hizb' as a cohesive political-spiritual bloc. The inclusion of Ashab al-Aykah alongside the more well-known Thamud and People of Lot underscores the universality of the rejection pattern across different prophetic eras. This categorization serves as a warning to the Quraysh that their denial places them in the same historical lineage of those who were eradicated for their arrogance.
